title: Don Giovanni
facts: Don Giovanni premiered in Prague at the National Theatre (today’s Estates Theatre) on 29 October 1787.
It was meant to open on 14 October 1787 for a visiting archduchess, but wasn’t ready, so Le Nozze di Figaro was played instead.
Prague commissioned it after Mozart’s successful visit there in early 1787.
The overture opens with a thundering D minor cadence and a mysterious passage, then turns into a light-hearted D major allegro.
The Catalogue Aria counts the Don’s conquests: 640 in Italy, 231 in Germany, 100 in France, 91 in Turkey, and in Spain, 1,003.
Thanks to this aria, German and other languages call fold-out brochures a “Leporello list”.
“Là ci darem la mano” (“There we will entwine our hands”): alone with Zerlina, the Don immediately turns on the charm.
The “Champagne Aria”: the Don orders a party with every girl Leporello can find.
Mozart added “Dalla sua pace” for the 1788 Vienna production, written for the tenor Francesco Morella.
Elvira’s “Mi tradì quell’alma ingrata” was also a Vienna addition, composed on 30 April 1788 for Caterina Cavalieri.
In Prague and Vienna one singer played both Masetto and the Commendatore. The demons’ chorus gave him just a little time to change costume.
Questo è il fin|Questo e il fin|Ah, dov.è il perfido
A memoirist claimed the final ensemble was heard only at the first Prague performance, then never again during the original run. Today it is almost always performed.
Kierkegaard argued that “among all classic works Don Giovanni stands highest.” Gounod called it “a work without blemish, of uninterrupted perfection”.
